why: Point prevalence is existing cases divided by the population at that point.

q: Cumulative incidence is best interpreted as:
options: Risk over a specified follow-up period
why: It is the proportion of initially at-risk people who develop the outcome over the stated period.

q: Fifteen new cases occur over 1,500 person-years. The rate per 1,000 person-years is:
Which measure depends strongly on prevalence?
why: PPV is affected by prevalence in the tested population.
